On a schedule you define — from seconds to years — FA periodically switches Wi-Fi, mobile data, and airplane mode off and back on, so your phone stops leaving a continuous, gap-free trail of where you are. Only in the intervals you choose, whenever you want. It also saves battery and can reboot the device on a timer. Everything runs locally; FA never connects to the internet.

Since Android 10, apps can no longer toggle Wi-Fi or mobile data directly, and rebooting needs elevated access too. FA needs either Shizuku (no root, paired once via Wireless Debugging) or root access to run these system commands.
Open Setup from the home screen banner. Shizuku needs no root — just a one-time pairing through Developer Options → Wireless Debugging. If your device is rooted, FA detects and uses it automatically.

Tap any rule on the home screen (Wi-Fi, mobile data, airplane mode, or reboot) to configure it: choose a mode, set how often it should cycle and for how long it stays on, then turn on the master switch to start.

An optional, root-only feature: pressing the power button 5 times sets a brand-new random password on your device and locks it immediately. This is risky — read the warnings on its setup screen carefully before arming it.

On a schedule you set, it periodically drops your connectivity (Wi-Fi / mobile data / airplane mode) and brings it back — so you are not continuously trackable without pause, and you save battery. It can also reboot the device periodically. Fully offline, no account, no tracking.
Why does it need Root or Shizuku?

Android has blocked regular apps from toggling Wi-Fi/mobile data since Android 10, and device reboot always requires elevated access. Root or Shizuku (a no-root, ADB-based permission bridge) are the only ways to run these system commands.
What\'s the difference between Root and Shizuku?

Root gives full system access via a root manager app (e.g. Magisk). Shizuku needs no root — you pair it once via Developer Options → Wireless Debugging — but its pairing may need restarting manually after a reboot on some devices, unless you enable Shizuku\'s own auto-start option.
Yes, if you leave the master switch on. With root, this is fully automatic. With Shizuku only, you may need to reopen the Shizuku app after a reboot unless its auto-start option is enabled.
No. FA has no internet permission at all — everything runs locally on your device.
What happens with Months/Years as a unit?
They\'re approximated as a fixed 30-day / 365-day duration for simplicity, not exact calendar months/years.

It carries a real risk of permanently locking you out of your device if something goes wrong. Read its setup screen warnings carefully, and test it on a spare device before ever arming it on your daily phone.
Why does my manufacturer keep killing the background service?
Some manufacturers (Xiaomi, Huawei, Oppo, etc.) restrict background apps beyond Android\'s own battery optimization. Check for an \"Autostart\" or \"Manage app launch\" setting and allow FA there.

The panic feature requires root — Shizuku is not supported for this feature.
The panic feature needs a privileged backend: root (recommended) or Shizuku (experimental). Neither is usable right now.

Without root the panic-lock runs over Shizuku, with weaker guarantees: (1) changing the lock-screen password from Shizuku is not guaranteed on every Android/OEM version — test it on a spare device before relying on it; (2) protection ENDS at reboot and does not re-arm automatically, because Shizuku is not running that early. For dependable protection, use root.

Read this before you arm:

• When triggered, a %1$d-character fully random password becomes your lock-screen password.
• Trigger = pressing the power button %2$d times within %3$d seconds.
• You MUST have saved that password somewhere outside this phone. If you lose it, you can be permanently locked out — possibly with data loss.
• After a trigger, the screen unlocks only with the new password.
• Backend: root is reliable; Shizuku is experimental and may not work on every device.

Only arm if you understand and accept this risk.
